summary: Initial audit has not established unauthorized access. Observed internet probes and successful staff/CI logins; investigating historical deploy-password access rather than assuming an unfamiliar address is malicious. Found excessive deploy sudo privileges, writable website code, and potentially unsafe maintenance/database credential handling. Auditing and repairing these while preserving staff access and scheduled shop jobs; continuing checks across all three servers.

Still no confirmed unauthorized access; Grafana traversal probes return 404 and application/SSH activity reviewed so far is consistent with shop work. Closed unrestricted deploy root-rsync access, root execution of website PHP in metrics, user-controlled root export-file writes, PHP execution in uploads/cache, unauthenticated support operations, writable web code, and root Git maintenance over developer-controlled configuration. CI release, maintenance, website/rental availability, mailing export, database reporting and payout check passed smoke tests. Staff authentication remains available; monitoring continues.

Contained coordinated backup-wiping nvega sessions on all three hosts: revoked the abused SSH keys globally and terminated the destructive forwarded session, retaining nvega's other key/password and other staff access. Repeat mobile-key login now fails. Reviewed sudo evidence shows deletion commands, not secret reads; no confirmed secret disclosure so far. Earlier application/privilege hardening remains in place; CI releases, website, reports, payouts and dump transfer continue.
